answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a refundable stake that remains locked until a randomly selected peer audits the result and challenges fraud. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity separately, so splitting one actor into many accounts does not multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk. A whisper network can coordinate audits, but a basalt-like record of stake, challenges, and slashing makes collusion costly to hide; the attacker pays in locked funds and forfeited deposits over a long horizon.
